"My calculations were perfect," he said. Mrs. Alvarez, the baker next door, chuckled. "Calculations are only half the recipe, dear. You have to taste the dough, and you have to be patient." On the third try, Bolt tasted the dough and added a pinch more sugar just because it felt right. When the cookies came out golden and soft, a tiny light on his chin blinked pink.

passage: In crowded cities, open land is scarce. Yet some builders have found an unexpected place to grow plants: the roof. Rooftop gardens, or green roofs, are spreading across the world.
